title: Physical hardware device record
$comment: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 ComradeArt — SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. Serial numbers, MAC addresses and any personally identifying device identifier must be redacted before commit; a record without operator and timestamps is refused (Stage-26 adversarial rule 17). This schema shapes the device record that FEEDS the release/hardware.py intake — it does not replace that gate, which additionally walks every string in a submission for identifier leaks and rejects the report if any is found. additionalProperties is false so that a fabricated or copy-pasted record with extra fields fails validation instead of slipping through.

manufacturer.$comment: The vendor name, e.g. a laptop maker. Never an asset tag or an owner.

model.$comment: The marketing model name. The model narrows the device to a product line, which the qualification needs; the serial narrows it to one unit, which it never needs.

motherboard.$comment: Board vendor and product name from DMI. board_serial must already be REDACTED by collect-hardware.sh.

firmwareVersion.$comment: Version strings are permitted to look serial-like; release/hardware.py allow-lists the firmwareVersion field for exactly this reason.

firmwareSettings.$comment: Setting name to value, e.g. secure-boot: enabled, tpm: enabled, sata-mode: ahci. Recorded because a test result is meaningless without the firmware configuration it was observed under: the same machine passes or fails secure-boot-development-path depending on a toggle.

storageDevice.$comment: Model name only. NVMe and SATA device serials are device identifiers and must be redacted.

tpm.$comment: spec is const 2.0 because the minimum target device requires TPM 2.0; a record for a device without one cannot validate, which is intended — that device is not the qualification target.

wifiDevice.$comment: Chipset or device name, never a MAC address and never a network name.

ethernetDevice.$comment: Chipset or device name, never a MAC address.

bluetoothDevice.$comment: Chipset or device name, never a Bluetooth address.

camera.$comment: Optional: a device may have no camera. Omitting the field means no camera was recorded; the test-run record for the camera-dependent tests then says NOT_PRESENT, which is a statement about the device, never a pass.

resolution.$comment: WIDTHxHEIGHT in pixels, e.g. 2256x1504. Needed to judge the hidpi-scaling test.

scale.$comment: The scale factor the session actually applied (1, 1.5, 2, ...).

battery.$comment: Optional: desktops have none. Record the class — chemistry and design capacity band — not the battery serial number, which upower and the kernel both expose and which must be redacted.

kernel.$comment: The uname -r string of the installed system under test.

driverVersions.$comment: Kernel module name to version, from modinfo of the loaded GPU and network modules. Driver names are classes, not identities.

installedArtifactDigest.$comment: The sha256 of the installed Bunny OS artifact, lower-case hex, no sha256: prefix. This is what binds the record to a build: physical evidence for an artifact nobody can name is not evidence. It is also the binding that makes the record physical — a DMI directory exists in a VM too, but a VM cannot honestly carry the digest of an image installed onto real firmware.

collectedAt.$comment: RFC 3339. Required without exception: a record without a timestamp is refused (Stage-26 adversarial rule 17).

collectedBy.$comment: The operator's name or handle — a person who can be asked what they saw. Required without exception: a record without an operator is refused (Stage-26 adversarial rule 17). Never a system username harvested from the device.

redactionStatus.$comment: Required, and there is deliberately no not-required value for hardware: every physical record passes through a redaction step. redacted means identifiers were found and removed; verified-clean means a human checked and found none. Either way, someone looked.
